<div class="proj-layout">
<div class="proj-main">
<section class="proj-q" aria-labelledby="h-question">
<h2 id="h-question"><i class="bi bi-question-circle" aria-hidden="true"></i>Research question</h2>
<p class="proj-question">How do electrolyzers, hydrogen storage and fuel cells change the cost, curtailment and firm output of a grid-connected wind farm?</p>
</section>
<section class="proj-sec" aria-labelledby="h-contribution">
<h2 id="h-contribution"><i class="bi bi-person-check" aria-hidden="true"></i>My contribution</h2>
<p>First author. Extended NREL&#x27;s REopt optimization model with hydrogen components and ran the analysis.</p>
</section>
<section class="proj-sec" aria-labelledby="h-method">
<h2 id="h-method"><i class="bi bi-diagram-3" aria-hidden="true"></i>Method</h2>
<p>Mixed-integer sizing and dispatch optimization for a 253-MW West Texas wind farm with ERCOT prices, with sensitivities to hydrogen price, region and future technology costs.</p>
</section>
<section class="proj-sec" aria-labelledby="h-findings">
<h2 id="h-findings"><i class="bi bi-lightbulb" aria-hidden="true"></i>Key findings</h2>
<ol class="findings">
<li>In the Journal of Mechanical Design case study, adding an electrolyzer reduced total system cost by about 7%.</li>
<li>In the same study, using hydrogen storage with fuel cells reduced it by about 26% and sharply cut curtailment (the earlier TORQUE 2022 case reported about 9% and 30%).</li>
</ol>
</section>
<section class="proj-sec proj-bounds" aria-labelledby="h-bounds">
<h2 id="h-bounds"><i class="bi bi-exclamation-circle" aria-hidden="true"></i>Boundary conditions</h2>
<p>Cost assumptions date from 2020–2023 and predate final federal hydrogen credit rules.</p>
</section>
